To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a cost-sensitive task-oriented framework is more effective in recognizing objects in real-world applications than state-of-the-art methods; (2) the proposed framework can generalize to new tasks for which no training data is available; and (3) a combination of linguistic and visual cues is more effective than using visual cues alone.

(1) we introduce the first task-oriented recognition method, (2) we introduce the concept of cost-sensitive recognition, and (3) we introduce a new dataset that is suitable for evaluating task-oriented recognition methods.

(a) we introduce the first task-oriented recognition dataset and a task-oriented recognition framework that generalizes to unseen tasks and (b) our task-oriented framework outperforms state of the art cost-sensitive recognition baselines.
